## Series Overview

I went through Andrew Ng's *Agentic AI* course on DeepLearning.AI mainly because
I kept hearing "agentic" thrown around at work without a shared definition, and
wanted a rigorous one before building anything else on top of Hermes Agent. The
course is good, but every example is generic — customer support bots, research
assistants. None of it touches what I actually do all day: segmenting voids and
lifted chips out of X-ray scans. So I rebuilt every example from scratch, in my
own domain, following the course's own five-module order — then kept going for
four more posts covering things the course doesn't touch at all but that I
think you need if you actually want to run this in production.

If you read all nine posts and work through the code, you should be able to go
from zero to building, hardening, and shipping your own agent.

### Posts in this series

**The course's own five modules, rebuilt around segmentation:**

1. [What Agentic AI Actually Is](01-applications.qmd) — the four design
   patterns (reflection, tool use, planning, multi-agent), the domain rules
   that make this a real problem instead of a toy one, and setting up aisuite.
2. [Reflection](02-reflection.qmd) — teaching an agent to catch a physically
   impossible segmentation mask (a void bigger than the chip it's in) before
   it reaches a KPI report, both self-critique and multimodal external critique.
3. [Tool Use and MCP](03-tool-use-mcp.qmd) — the biggest post in the series:
   aisuite's automatic tool-calling, the manual tool-calling loop, and a full
   MCP server so Copilot, Cursor, and Claude Code can call the same tools
   directly.
4. [Evaluations and Error Analysis](04-evaluation-error-analysis.qmd) — the
   module Andrew Ng himself calls the most valuable: the component-tagging
   method for turning a vague "the model isn't great" into a ranked, concrete
   list of what to fix next.
5. [Planning and Multi-Agent Systems](05-planning-multiagent.qmd) — JSON plans
   vs. code-as-plan, and the two ends of the multi-agent spectrum: a
   predictable linear pipeline and a chaos-tolerant all-to-all team.

**Four posts past the course, covering what it takes to actually ship this:**

6. [Advanced Agentic AI Development](06-advanced-agentic-development.qmd) —
   retries, timeouts, cost tracking, memory, prompt-injection defenses,
   automated testing, Docker/systemd deployment, OpenTelemetry tracing, a real
   HITL queue, and prompt/config versioning. The longest post in the series.
7. [Agent-to-Agent Interoperability with A2A](07-a2a-interoperability.qmd) —
   Google's A2A protocol for when independent agents, built by different teams
   in different frameworks, need to talk to each other as peers, not as a tool
   call.
8. [Fine-Tuning and Distilling Your Own Agent](08-finetuning-distillation.qmd)
   — logging real production traffic, filtering out human-corrected examples,
   and LoRA fine-tuning a small local model to reproduce a large model's agent
   decisions cheaply, with a staged rollout.
9. [Retrieval, Grounding Your Agent in Real Knowledge](09-retrieval-rag.qmd) —
   two different retrieval problems (visual case similarity vs. textual spec
   knowledge), plus why whole-image similarity and defect-crop similarity need
   separate embedding spaces to be useful.

## Tools used throughout

- [aisuite](https://github.com/andrewyng/aisuite) as the model-provider layer
  — one interface, so the same agent code runs against a cloud model or a
  local Qwen3 endpoint on my own GX10 with a one-line change
- MCP (Model Context Protocol) and A2A (Agent2Agent) for, respectively,
  agent-to-tool and agent-to-agent interoperability
- DINOv3 + LanceDB for visual case retrieval, `sentence-transformers` for
  textual spec retrieval
- Real semiconductor-imaging domain rules throughout: p2/p98 percentile X-ray
  normalization, chip-containment checks, IoU-based evals

:::{.callout-note}
This series pairs well with the [Local-AI Defect Inspection Series](../local-ai-defect-inspection/index.qmd),
which covers fine-tuning and evaluating small local VLMs on the same class of
imagery.
:::
